# Kit API (generated by scripts/api.mjs from kit/scripts/lib/reel-lib.cjs; don't edit by hand)

Scene files: `module.exports = (L, s, reel) => ({ lift, svg, html, anim, over?, cam?, fade?, boxes?, overlapOk? })`.
`s` = `{ id, p, n, line, start, dur, words, at(word, nth) }`; every cue time comes from `s.at()` (script/cues.md lists them).
Prefix every id with `s.p`. `boxes: [{ id, r: [x, y, w, h], t?: [t0, t1] }]` (in .lift coords) are checked by build-scenes
for overlaps and for leaving the grid field; duplicate ids fail the build. DESIGN.md says how things look, this file what exists.

## Timeline helpers (inside a scene's `anim`, which runs with `tl`, `q`, `E`, `gsap` in scope)

- `seg(e, a, b)` a slice [a, b] of an ease, renormalised: the two sides of a cut play seg(e, 0, f) and seg(e, f, 1)
- `slide(s, at, dx = 40, dy = -23, dur = 0.55)`
- `fadeUp(s, at, d = 10, dur = 0.35)`
- `draw(s, at, dur = 0.5)`
- `untrim(s, at, dur = 0.35, st = 0)` trims tween the stroke-dashoffset ATTRIBUTE: the CSS property snaps to whole numbers under pathLength="1" trim off: the stroke retracts from its start toward its end (hidden once retracted: a round cap still paints a dot at a zero-length dash)
- `wipe(s, at, dur = 0.38)`
- `unwipe(s, at, dur = 0.3)`
- `pop(s, at)`
- `unpop(s, at)`
- `lead(id, at)`
- `unlead(id, at)`
- `wipeIn(s, at, dur = 0.5, st = 0)` clip reveals: left -> right in, and out toward the right
- `wipeOut(s, at, dur = 0.28, st = 0)`
- `kin(s, at, st = 0.05, dur = 0.6)` kinetic type: masked words rise in (and leave upward)
- `kout(s, at, st = 0.03, dur = 0.32)`
- `type(s, at, cps = 0.04)` typed value: one character every cps seconds; untype removes them last-first
- `untype(s, at, cps = 0.03)`
- `plateIn(s, at, dur = 0.5)` label plate: the frame wipes in, the name rises in its mask
- `away(s, at, dy = -24, dur = 0.3, st = 0)`
- `drift(s, at, dur, dy, dx = 0)` parallax plane: a group drifts against the camera, a few px, settling with it (never longer than SETTLE)
- `run(s, at, dur = 0.7, reps = 0, gap = 0)` data pulse (pulse() in the lib): the segment runs the tube start -> end at an even pace
- `mfSet(id, r)`
- `morph(id, A, B, at, dur, ease)`
- `dropIn(s, at, o = {})` drop-in (DESIGN.md 5.8 "assemble bottom-up"): an element or a list falls dy px into place with a short fade. The from-state is set once at build and both moves are .to tweens, so the pair never trips gsap_repeated_fromto_without_baseline. o = { dy (-40), dur (0.5), fade (0.1), stagger (0), ease (E.out) }
- `assemble(s, at, o = {})` a crafted object's parts, bottom-up (pass its parts list: assemble(q("#a-p0, #a-p1"), at))
- `swapName(id, at, dur = 0.36)` swapPlate()'s roll: the old name rises out of the mask as the new one rises in; the old tag (if any) pops out
- `flow(s, pts, at, dur, reps)` packet cube travels a sampled path, looping with an even pace

## Basics

- `fs` repo-reel scene library: every object, helper and the scene shell from the v3 MultiPath reel, plus the v4 motion layer (HarnessRouter reel: custom eases, match-cut handoffs, morph frames, kinetic type, trims, pulses, motion blur), crafted objects drawn with the Anatomy geometry kit (selector, board; see anat.cjs), and v5 (UncensoredAi reel: the implode-to-a-seed cut and the frame chrome the bg composition draws). Scene files in scripts/scenes/ receive this as `L`. Geometry uses assets/js/iso.js; colours come only from T.
- `path`
- `r1(n)`
- `txt(x, y, s, o = {})`
- `label(id, x, y, lines, o = {})`
  - ids: #id (svg g) · starts: visible (static text; use klabel to animate)
- `lead(id, pts)` leader drawn on with dashoffset; arrowhead pops at the end
  - ids: #id-l (line), #id-h (arrowhead) · starts: drawn; lead(id, at) brings it on from hidden, unlead(id, at) takes it off
- `dtube(id, d, o)` a tube whose two strokes draw on together
  - ids: #id (g) holding two pathLength=1 paths · starts: drawn; draw(q("#id path"), at) brings it on from hidden, untrim(q("#id path"), at) retracts it
- `barrow(id, x, y, len, ang, fill, o)` block arrow wrapped so it can wipe in from its tail
  - ids: #id (g) · starts: visible; wipe("#id", at) / unwipe
- `cube(id, s = 22)` lime packet cube centred on (0,0); moved with x/y keyframes
  - ids: #id · starts: hidden (opacity 0); flow() shows and moves it
- `bez(p, t)`
- `bpath(p)`
- `samples(p, a = 0, b = 1, n = 16)`
- `nsv`

## motion v4 (HarnessRouter reel): custom eases, match cuts, morphs, kinetic type, trims, pulses

- `BZ_SRC` Cubic-bezier solver (CSS semantics). Every ease below keeps y inside 0..1, so nothing overshoots (DESIGN.md 7). The same source runs in Node (to plan handoffs) and in each scene's timeline (as GSAP ease functions).
- `EZ` the reel's easing set (control points). out: UI entrances; outQ: softer settle; inOut: parts moving between rests; in: exits (accelerate away); ramp: speed-ramped handoffs (slow-fast-slow, the cut sits near peak speed); cam: camera drift; flow: trim paths / tubes drawing on.
- `bz`
- `E`
- `r2(n)`
- `r3(n)`
- `CAM_O` camera: .cam scales about (540, 864) (50% 45% of the frame) and translates by (x, y)
- `SETTLE` camera and parallax moves settle within SETTLE s, then hold: a slow sub-pixel crawl across a whole scene makes every thin outline shimmer (its antialiasing shifts frame to frame, worst in a scaled-down player)
- `camOf(c)`
- `toScreen(c, lift, r)` a rect [x, y, w, h] in a scene's .lift coords -> screen coords, under camera state c
- `placeAt(c, lift, lx, ly, S, k = 1)` GSAP {x, y, scale} (transform-origin 0 0) that puts an element whose CSS top-left is (lx, ly) in .lift at screen point S with screen scale k, under camera state c
- `lerp(a, b, t)`
- `lerpR(A, B, t)`

## handoff: an object-based match cut

- `handoff({ A, B, t0, cut, land, ease = "ramp" })` One object (a morph frame or a real element) travels from screen rect A (scene N) to screen rect B (scene N+1). The whole move is ONE eased curve over T = land - t0 (global seconds); the cut at fraction f splits it: scene N plays seg(ease, 0, f), scene N+1 plays seg(ease, f, 1), so position AND velocity match across the cut. Snap `land` to a music beat so the object settles on the beat.
- `segEase(h, side)`
- `carry(sel, h, side, o, at)` a real element carried across the cut (not a morph frame). A/B/M of the handoff are its screen top-left points. o = { lx, ly, lift, cam } for this side: (lx, ly) = its CSS top-left in .lift; cam = the camera state while it moves (the end state on the out side; null on the in side, where the camera starts after the landing). Its screen scale follows the camera: s on the out side, 1 on the in side.
- `morphCode(id, h, side, at, show)` morph-frame code for one side of a handoff: out = swap the source for the frame at `at`, move A -> M until the cut; in = frame starts at M, lands on B, then swaps for the target (`show`: selector set visible on landing)

## morph frame: a window outline that changes size and place (DESIGN.md 7 "Morph": parts move, no blob tweening)

- `MB(n = 12)` Five transform-only parts (fill + four 2.5px edges), each motion-blurred on its own, so the smear follows size changes too. Lives in the stage's screen layer (`over`) for cross-cut handoffs, or inside .lift for a morph within one scene.
- `mframe(id)`
  - ids: #id, parts #id-f/-t/-b/-l/-r · starts: zero size (invisible); mfSet / morph / morphCode place and move it
- `trimRect(id, x, y, w, h)` a window's outline drawn as a trim path: two halves start at the top-left corner and meet bottom-right
  - ids: #id (g) with two paths · starts: hidden (dashoffset 1); draw(q("#id path"), at)
- `appWinC(id, x, y, w, h, title, inner, o = {})` app window whose chrome + contents sit in one layer (#id-c), so the contents can wipe out and leave the bare outline (the outline is what a morph frame picks up at a match cut). o.attr: extra attributes on the window (e.g. MB()).
  - ids: #id (.win), #id-c (chrome + contents layer) · starts: visible; wipeIn("#id-c", at) / wipeOut("#id-c", at) leaves the bare outline
- `hlTrim(id, x, y, w, h)` highlight box drawn as a trim path (lime 4px with dark edges) around a screenshot region; HTML, place it inside the window
  - ids: #id (svg), paths #id-u (dark edge) and #id-o (lime) · starts: hidden; draw(q("#id path"), at) / untrim(q("#id path"), at)
- `pulse(id, d, o = {})` data pulse: a short segment running inside a tube's core. Neutral pulses are one `dark` stroke; lime pulses get a dark edge (on 10 under lime 6) like every lime shape. len = fraction of the path.
  - ids: #id (g, data-len) · starts: hidden; run("#id", at, dur, reps, gap)
- `kword(w)` one masked word (the unit kin / kout move); the mask is meant to clip, so the layout audit is told so
  - ids: none (.km mask > .kw word) · starts: visible
- `klabel(id, x, y, lines, o = {})` kinetic label: same type as label() (Inter 400 30px caps, 0.04em, 36px leading), each word in a mask so kin() can rise it. (x, y) is the first baseline, like txt(). a: "start" | "middle" | "end".
  - ids: #id, words .kw inside · starts: visible; kin("#id", at) keeps the words hidden until they rise, kout / L.kspan take them off
- `typed(id, text)` typed value: characters rise in one by one inside a mask (no caret needed); type() / untype() drive it. "--" stays one unit: split apart, the two inline-block hyphens lose their kerning and read as "- -"
  - ids: #id, characters .kw inside · starts: visible; type("#id", at, cps) keeps them hidden until they type in
- `beatGrid(grids)` music beat grid: beats(bpm, phase) -> snap(t) = the nearest beat to t (global seconds); pass several grids as [[from, bpm, phase], ...] when the bed restarts mid-reel

## crafted objects (Anatomy kit via anat.cjs; DESIGN.md 5.8)

- `anat(ox, oy, u)` Built from real parts (base, bevel, seam, screws, glands, lamps), drawn in the 3 flat tones with ink outlines. Each returns { svg, ...ids and screen points } so a scene can wire tubes to its ports and animate its parts.
- `selector(id, ox, oy, u = 1.3)` rotary selector: base on feet, housing with two output glands (+y = port 0, lower-left; +x = port 1, lower-right) and a lamp each, detent scale, collar, knob with grip ring + pointer, input coupling on the axis. (ox, oy) = axis on the ground; u = size. ids: parts `${id}-p0..p4` (bottom-up), pointer `${id}-ptr` (gsap.set svgOrigin "0 0"; rotation 0 = port 0, -90 = port 1), lamps `${id}-lp0/1`. Points: top (input enters here, from above), ports [tip0, tip1].
- `board(id, ox, oy, mark = "HR", u = 1)` router board: standoffs, bevelled board with seam, vent slots, screws and traces; a chip (mark) with pins; two capacitors and an input socket. Three output glands, each with a lamp: port 0 and 1 on the +y face (lower-left), port 2 on the +x face (lower-right). (ox, oy) = the board's back corner on the ground (same footprint as adapter()).
  - ids: parts `${id}-hp0..hp2` (board, chip, small parts), lamps `${id}-lmp0..2`. Points: sock (input, from above), ports.

## shell

- `CSS`
- `limeEdges(m)`
- `scene(o)`
- `sceneRaw({ id, p, dur, lift, svg, html = "", anim, over = "", cam, fade = true })` over: HTML in the stage's screen layer (above the camera; morph frames of cross-cut handoffs live here). cam: { s, x, y, t0, t1 } = one eased camera move to (scale s, offset x/y) over local t0..t1 (default: the v3 push to 1.03, settled within SETTLE). fade: false for scenes that hand off to the next one through a match cut (nothing to clear: the cut is the transition).

## word cues

- `keyOf(w)` Scene objects come from build-scenes.cjs: { id, p, n, line, start, dur, words, at(word, nth) }. at() returns the scene-local time of the nth spoken occurrence of `word` (case/punctuation-insensitive), so every pop lands on its word. It throws if the word is missing, so a script edit never silently desyncs.
- `makeCues(all, sc)`

## fixed CTA scene (DESIGN.md 6.1)

- `ctaScene(sc, cfg)` cfg: { url, trust: [{ text, kind: "x" | undefined, word }...] (all but the last go on top, the last under the device), device?: (id, ox, oy) => svg (default laptop; false = no device), glyph?: laptop screen glyph fn or a GLYPHS name ("merge" | "fan"), shotH?: crop height of repo-header.png at 2560 wide, follow?: word that starts "Follow for more useful tools" (default "follow") } The last trust item may carry code: ["line", ...] (e.g. the install command): beat A then moves up to make room and a Terminal window under that plate types the lines in while its sentence is spoken.
- `ctaRects(cfg)` the CTA's layout rects (the same geometry as ctaScene): n1 = the first trust plate (where a match cut lands; use L.ctaRects(reel.cta).n1 as the plan's R rect), pc = the last plate, code = its Terminal (or null), device = { ox, oy } (or null), repo = the repo window. All [x, y, w, h] in the CTA's .lift (lift 0).
- `ctaCut(sc, reel, o = {})` v4 CTA (DESIGN.md 6.1 "v4 CTA motion"): ctaScene's layout and config (reel.json -> cta), plus a match cut in. o = { inbound: the plan's handoff into this scene (P.inbound("cta")), or null for no cut; cam: P.cam("cta") }. The handoff lands as the first trust plate (its name rises on its word); later plates wipe in on their words; the device slides in and its glyph draws; a Terminal (last item's code) wipes in on that item's word and types. On the follow word everything clears and the Terminal's frame (else the first plate's) grows into the repo window, then the URL, "Follow for more useful tools" (fixed text), the underline and the Follow click. Scene file: module.exports = (L, s, reel) => { const P = require("./_plan.cjs"); return L.ctaCut(s, reel, { inbound: P.inbound("cta"), cam: P.cam("cta") }); };
- `todoScene(sc)` placeholder for a scene whose file doesn't exist yet (shows up in preview so nothing is forgotten)

## more objects + motion (Paseo reel)

- `screenWin(id, x, y, w, h, screens, o = {})` screen frame: a bare 2.5px ink outline (no title bar: DESIGN.md 5.7) whose inside is a viewport (#id-v, overflow hidden) holding one or more screens (#sid, absolute, top-left). A screen = { id, src, w, h, x?, y?, inner?, attr? }: inner = extra HTML that moves with it (trim boxes that zoom with the shot); attr = extra attributes (MB() for screens that push). #id-o = a fixed layer over the screens (o.over: trim boxes that don't zoom). The viewport sits in #id-c, so wipeOut("#id-c") leaves the bare outline for a morph frame. Viewport size: (w - 5) x (h - 5).
  - ids: #id (.win), #id-c (wipe layer), #id-v (viewport), #id-o (fixed over layer), each screen #<sid> · starts: visible
- `fitShot(ar, vw, vh, mode = "width")` screen size for a shot of aspect ar in a viewport vw x vh: "width" fills the width (crops the bottom), "cover" fills both
- `shotBox(id, x, y, w, h, src, o = {})` bare framed shot (a phone screen, a logo tile): .win box (2.5px ink edge) with the image (#id-i) filling it, in #id-c. pad = inset of the image as a fraction of the box (logo tiles; the image keeps its aspect).
  - ids: #id (.win), #id-c (wipe layer), #id-i (img) · starts: visible
- `agentWin(id, x, y, w, h, title, logo, o = {})` agent window: its logo, placeholder rows, a lime progress bar (#id-pf, grows with scaleX); contents in #id-c
  - ids: #id, #id-c, lime bar #id-pf (full width: tween scaleX 0 -> 1) · starts: visible
- `rails(id, trunk, branches, nodes)` branch rails: a git graph. trunk = path d, branches = [d, ...] (neutral tubes that draw on, each with a lime twin #id-g<i> that draws over it when changes flow down it), nodes = [[x, y], ...] commit dots #id-n<k> that pop as the trim passes.
  - ids: trunk #id-t, branches #id-b<i>, lime twins #id-g<i>, commit dots #id-n<k> · starts: all visible and drawn; draw() / pop() them in
- `dimLine(id, x1, x2, y, tick = 20)` dimension line: a measured span with end ticks; the line (#id-l0/l1) trims out from its centre, the ticks (#id-a/b) pop
  - ids: half lines #id-l0/l1, ticks #id-a/b · starts: lines hidden (dashoffset 1), ticks visible; draw() the lines, pop() the ticks

## timeline code builders (strings for a scene's anim)

- `stretch(sels, dA, dB, at, dur, ease = "E.inOut")` stretch tether: a live tube (and the pulses riding it) re-routes as the thing it is tied to moves. Every path under the selectors gets its d tweened A -> B (same command structure, so GSAP interpolates each number).
- `lensIn(box, mf, inset, src, dst, at, dur = 0.45)` detail lens: a trim box draws on a region of a shot (box = an hlTrim id), then a morph frame (mf, an mframe in .lift) lifts out of that region and opens into the inset (a shotBox showing the region magnified), which appears as the frame lands, its image settling from a slight push. src / dst = [x, y, w, h] in .lift coords.
- `lensOut(box, inset, at)`
- `converge(items, pt, at, dur = 0.42, st = 0.05, k = 0.25)` converge into a window: each item [sel, x, y, w] (CSS top-left and width of a square item in .lift) flies its centre to point pt, shrinking to scale k about its centre (the same origin pop() uses, so scrubbing never jumps) and accelerating in (E.in), staggered, and is hidden on arrival. Give the items MB() and static contents.
- `pushScreens(a, b, vw, at, dur = 0.55)` screen push: screen a leaves left as screen b enters from the right (one eased move; give both MB())
- `zoomIn(sel, at, s, ox, oy, dur = 0.7, from = 1)` zoom inside a window: the screen scales about (ox, oy) (px in its own coords) while the frame stays put

## v5 (UncensoredAi reel): implode-to-a-seed cut and frame chrome (DESIGN.md 4 "Frame chrome", 7 "Implode")

- `flatPath(d)` The implode needs a seed (a spark: a lime dot with a ping ring) that the next scene draws its first lines away from, so the spark and its path sampler live here too. Path sampler: points evenly spaced by arc length along an SVG path d (M L H V C Z, absolute or relative). A spark's keyframes come from it, so the head sits exactly on the trim's front at every frame (both use the same ease over the same length).
- `pathPts(d, n = 28)`
- `spark(id)` spark: a lime dot with a dark edge (#id-d) and a ping ring (#id-r). It is the implode's seed, and after the cut it rides the front of the trims that grow out of the seed (sdraw), so the first object is drawn by that point. Place it in the same svg as the paths it draws.
  - ids: #id, dot #id-d, ring #id-r · starts: hidden; sparkRun / sdraw / ping show it
- `sparkRun(id, d, at, dur = 0.5, o = {})` code builders (strings for a scene's anim) the head runs path d from at to at + dur with the same ease as the trim (E.flow by default), then pings and hides
- `ping(id, at, r = 30)` the ring opens round the head's position and fades (one ping, never a loop)
- `sdraw(head, sel, d, at, dur = 0.5, o = {})` draw a trim (a dtube's group, or any selector of pathLength="1" paths) led by a spark along d
- `seed(p)` implode to a seed: the whole scene (its .lift) shrinks into one screen point and leaves a lime seed there, which the next scene grows its first line from (point -> line -> object). For a turn in the argument ("but here's the catch"). pt = screen point; lift and cam = this scene's lift and its camera state at the implode.
  - ids: #<p>-sd (a spark in the screen layer) · starts: hidden; implode / seedIn place and show it
- `implode(p, at, pt, lift, cam, dur = 0.36)`
- `seedIn(p, pt)` the receiving side: the seed sits at pt on frame 0 and pings, then (in the scene) its sparks draw away from it
- `odo(id, value, lh)` odometer digits: each digit is a masked column 0-9 0-9 that rolls (E.inOut) to its next value, so a number changes by rolling, not by a swap. Tabular figures, any font size; lh = line height in px.
  - ids: #id-d<i>, one column per digit · starts: every column shows 0, not `value`: gsap.set("#id-d<i>", { y: -digit * lh }) first, or roll(..., first = true)
- `roll(id, a, b, lh, at, dur = 0.5, first = false)` roll digits from value a to b (same length); each digit moves forward (9 -> 0 passes through 10)
- `chrome(scenes, total)` frame chrome (bg composition): registration marks just outside the grid field's corners and a figure readout under it ("FIG. 03 / 12", the number rolling at every cut, with one segment per scene that fills as the reel advances), like the margins of a technical manual's page. No accent; it never moves except on a cut.

## build-time guards and planning (Harness2 reel)

- `hold(tin, tout, min = 0.6, what = "element")` Each helper here turns a mistake that used to surface only in a snapshot or a check warning into an error at build time, with the fix in the message. hold check for an in/out pair taken from two words: returns tout, or throws when out comes less than min s after in (a label that flashes, or an exit that cuts off its own entrance)
- `wordCount(lines)`
- `kspan(sel, n, tin, tout, o = {})` kinetic label in AND out as one call (anim code): the rise must finish, plus o.hold s (default 0.3), before the exit. n = the label's word count, or its lines (as passed to klabel). o = { st (0.05), dur (0.5), hold (0.3), ost (kout stagger) }
- `swapPlate(id, x, y, w, from, to, kind)` plate whose name rolls from one value to another (DESIGN.md 7 "Value or state swap"); swapName(id, at) runs the roll. Both names share one mask and the longer one sets its width, so neither is clipped. kind = the tag shown with the first value ("none" = no tag); it pops out as the name rolls. ids: #id-a (from), #id-b (to), #id-tag.
  - starts: shows `from` (and its tag); swapName(id, at) rolls it
- `regionOf(rect, srcW, sw, o = {})` screenshot region: rect [x, y, w, h] in the source image's own pixels (as read off the PNG) -> px in the shot as shown (srcW = the file's width, sw = its shown width from fitShot), and optionally after zoomIn(s, origin) inside its window. Use the result for hlTrim boxes (in the window's fixed over layer when the shot is zoomed).
- `boundsOf(pts)` shapes for a scene's `boxes` (build-scenes checks them): a rect [x, y, w, h], or a convex outline [[x, y], ...]. boundsOf = the rect round some points; hullOf = their convex outline; isoHull = the silhouette of an iso box make(ox, oy).box(x, y, z, w, d, h), a hexagon: use it for iso objects, whose rects overlap at the corners when the objects themselves don't. isoBounds = that box's rect.
- `hullOf(pts)`
- `isoHull(...a)`
- `isoBounds(...a)`
- `plan(timing, o = {})` cut plan factory: the v4 `_plan.cjs` machinery in one call, so a reel's plan only declares data. timing = script/timing.json. o = { keys: scene keys in order (default: each scene's line id), lift: { key: px } (default 0), camEnd: { key: { s, x, y } } (default { s: 1.03 }; hold-cut sources default { s: 1 }), R: { name: [x, y, w, h] } rects in each scene's .lift that the cuts connect, hands: { h1: [from, to, rectA, rectB, t0, land] } rect = an R name or an array; cut = to's start; land snaps to the nearest music beat (o.snap: false keeps it as given), holds: [[from, to], ...] hold cuts: the same frame on both sides, so from's camera must end at rest and both lifts match } Returns { KEYS, start, dur, beat, lift, camEnd, R, H, scr, hand, cam(key, { t0 }), side(key, rect, side), inbound, outbound, report (one row per hand: out / in side, f, issues, fix), table() (that report as text; build-scenes prints it and warns on every hand whose side or f is out of range, with a t0 / land that fits) }.

## CSS classes (the scene shell's stylesheet, usable in any scene's html)

- `.lift` the scene's art layer; its top = the scene's lift
- `.art` the full-frame svg inside .lift (the scene's svg string)
- `.win` window or screenshot frame: hi fill, 2.5px ink edge; border-box, so it holds (w - 5) x (h - 5)
- `.win-bar` a drawn window's 46px title bar (drawn windows only, never over a screenshot)
- `.win-ph` placeholder block in a drawn window (g300)
- `.win-ph.lt` the light placeholder tone (g100)
- `.plate` label plate, 68px tall; plate() builds it
- `.row` a 700 x 68 checklist row (icon tile + plate)
- `.ico` 68px icon tile slot
- `.pbar` progress bar track
- `.pfill` lime progress fill (tween scaleX)
- `.code` code / terminal / field text: Inter 500 24px, pre, tabular (set font-size inline to change)
- `.rate` data readout: Inter 600 30px, tabular
- `.cursor` the pointer svg (POINTER)
- `.ctr` full-width row that centres its child (CTA url, follow line)
- `.url` the CTA url plate
- `.ftxt` the CTA follow line, Inter 600 56px
- `.over` the stage's screen layer above the camera (a scene's over html)
- `.pt` a plate's name mask
- `.klab` kinetic label text (klabel builds it)
- `.km` a word or character mask (kword, typed, odo)
- `.kw` the masked unit kin / kout / type move
- `.hlt` trim highlight box svg (hlTrim)
- `.wc` a window's contents layer (#id-c), the thing wipeIn / wipeOut clip
- `.plane` full-frame group that drifts as one parallax plane (drift)

## From assets/js/iso.js (re-exported)

- `T` the colour tokens (DESIGN.md 2): never hard-code a hex in a scene. `C`, `S` = cos 30 and sin 30.
- `make(ox, oy)` the 30-degree projector: `{ P(x, y, z), poly, quad, line, box(x, y, z, w, d, h, { top, left, right, sw }), face, topFace, yFace, xFace, disc, knob }`. x runs down-right, y down-left, z up; the face functions give an SVG transform for drawing flat on a face.
- `tube(d, { w, fill })` double-line cable; `arrow(x, y, len, angle, fill)` block arrow; `leader(points)` a static leader; `check(x, y, s, sw)` a check mark.
